summary: This excerpt from Book 14 (part 144) is a fiction scene in which a narrator, working with Danny, Jack, Marsh and Sarah, pretends to help two men plan an attack. Jack and Marsh bring a backpack of explosive-looking material and ask Danny to plan bombing targets such as a bridge, Union Station, a precinct house, or tank cars carrying combustible fuel through Minneapolis. The narrator steers the conversation and then reveals that Danny is a sting participant, and Jack and Marsh are exposed as the scene ends with Sarah confronting them with her camera.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, a narrator and Danny pretend to help Jack and Marsh plan bombings, then expose them as Sarah confronts the pair on camera.
key_facts: Jack and Marsh lift a backpack and set it on the table as a sample for Danny to examine.
The narrator says putting explosives under cop cars 'came up last night' and proposes bombing the precinct house on Lake Street.
Marsh asks Danny whether a bridge or Union Station would be doable.
Marsh refers to the I-35 bridge and says it is too strategic with too many cameras.
Danny suggests tank cars coming in from North Dakota as targets because their contents are highly combustible.
Danny claims the old tankers travel right through Minneapolis and are basically rolling bombs.
Danny says that with what is in the backpack one could reduce a whole neighborhood to smoking ruin.
The narrator grabs an object resembling a white sausage from the backpack and Danny stops them from handling it further.
Marsh says the amount of material needed depends on the target and he must do the calculations.
Jack tells Marsh that Simon was right and Danny knows his stuff.
The narrator announces loudly that Danny is a far better actor than Jack and Marsh and that they know what is really going on.
Jack congratulates Danny, saying he did brilliantly.
Marsh jumps out of his chair swearing.
Sarah pulls the curtain aside, strides out, and points her camera at Jack and Marsh while firing questions.
